description: A focused information pack for Huntington's disease, HTT genetics, symptoms, research, clinical trials and life with the condition. It is an information-discovery aid, not medical advice.

synopsis.overview: Huntington's disease (HD) is an inherited neurodegenerative condition caused by a disease-associated expansion in the HTT gene. Progressive changes in brain cells can affect movement, thinking, mood and behaviour.
synopsis.manifestations: Symptoms vary and may include involuntary movements, stiffness, impaired coordination, changes in speech or swallowing, difficulties with planning and concentration, depression, irritability or other psychiatric symptoms. Juvenile-onset disease can have a different pattern and progression.
synopsis.management: There is currently no cure. Specialist multidisciplinary care may include medicines for movement or psychiatric symptoms, physiotherapy, occupational and speech therapy, nutritional and swallowing support, mental-health care, advance planning and genetic counselling. Predictive testing should be undertaken through an appropriate genetics service.
synopsis.outlook: HD is lifelong and progressive, but its timing, symptoms and rate of change vary widely. Research includes disease-modifying, gene-targeted and symptom-focused approaches. A personal outlook should be discussed with the treating team and should not be inferred from a search result or family history alone.

topics.heading: Clinical trials
topics.description: Registered Huntington's disease studies, including gene-targeted, antisense, biomarker, rehabilitation and symptom-treatment research. A listing does not indicate eligibility or recommendation.

topics.heading: Treatment and symptom care
topics.description: Medicines and multidisciplinary care addressing movement, mood, thinking, swallowing, communication, nutrition, mobility and daily function in Huntington's disease.

termDefinitions.tetrabenazine: A medicine used in some settings to reduce chorea; suitability and monitoring require clinical advice.
termDefinitions.chorea: Involuntary, irregular, flowing movements that may occur in Huntington disease.

topics.heading: Research and innovation
topics.description: Research into HTT biology, CAG repeats, disease mechanisms, biomarkers, gene silencing, gene therapy, neuroprotection, cognition and care approaches.

topics.heading: Genetics and testing
topics.description: HTT inheritance, CAG repeats, family risk, genetic counselling, predictive testing and reproductive options; results require qualified interpretation.

termDefinitions.HTT gene: The gene in which a disease-associated CAG repeat expansion causes Huntington disease.
termDefinitions.HTT CAG repeat: A repeated DNA sequence in the HTT gene; its length is interpreted by a genetics service in clinical context.
termDefinitions.genetic counselling: A specialist process explaining inherited-condition risks, testing choices, results and family-planning considerations.
termDefinitions.predictive testing: Testing an asymptomatic person with relevant family risk to determine whether a disease-associated genetic change is present; it requires specialist counselling.

topics.heading: Living with Huntington's disease
topics.description: Daily life, movement and communication support, mental wellbeing, relationships, work, activities, nutrition, safety and future planning for people living with HD.

topics.heading: Family and caregiving
topics.description: Information for families and care partners about changing needs, communication, support services, safeguarding, respite and care coordination.

topics.heading: Advocacy and access
topics.description: Patient organisations, research participation, public awareness, equitable access to specialist services, disability inclusion and community support.
